channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Effectiveness of Telerehabilitation Versus Conventional Rehabilitation on Motor Function and Activities of Daily Living After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of four RCTs (n=226) found telerehabilitation to be non-inferior to conventional physiotherapy for improving motor function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment) and activities of daily living (Barthel Index) in stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Body Acupuncture, Electroacupuncture, and Auricular Acupuncture in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found acupuncture significantly improved motor function in stroke survivors compared to controls (SMD=6.48; 95% CI=4.72-8.24; P<0.001), with electroacupuncture showing the greatest efficacy among body, electro-, and auricular acupuncture.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness and feasibility of home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases were effective in improving aerobic capacity, functional capacity, muscle strength, and quality of life, and were feasible, although reporting quality varied.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Beyond the Diagnosis: An Integrated Perspective on Strategic Dosing in Neurologic Motor Rehabilitation. A Scoping Review and Collaborative Viewpoint.
item.description: This scoping review and collaborative viewpoint propose an integrated, mechanism-based framework for strategic dosing in neurologic motor rehabilitation, suggesting higher intensity for non-progressive conditions and conservative strategies for progressive conditions, to address suboptimal long-term outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of a Personalized Robot-Assisted Trunk and Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Patients with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=40) found that adding personalized robot-assisted trunk and lower limb training to conventional rehabilitation significantly improved Functional Ambulatory Category (FAC) scores in patients with chronic stroke over 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical and mental health-related quality of life outcomes of non-pharmacological interventions in early multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found non-pharmacological interventions to improve physical and mental health-related quality of life in adults with early-stage multiple sclerosis and minimal disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the effectiveness and optimal dosage of physical exercise on cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: A two-phase study found that neuromuscular training with augmented low-dye taping (NMT + ALDT) was more effective in the short term for pronation-related anterior knee pain compared to routine physiotherapy care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of In-Clinic Rehabilitation vs. Home-Based Telerehabilitation for Adults with MS in the Deep South: The TEAMS Cluster Randomized Trial.
item.description: The TEAMS cluster-randomized trial of 759 adults with MS found no significant difference in effectiveness between a 12-week complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) program delivered in-clinic by a therapist (DirectCAM, n=382) versus self-initiated at home via telerehabilitation (TeleCAM, n=377).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesized evidence on arm exercise training for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), confirming its role as a component of pulmonary rehabilitation for managing extrapulmonary features.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Joint non-linear dose-response associations of device-measured physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness with cardiovascular disease: a cohort and Mendelian randomisation study
item.description: A UK Biobank cohort study with Mendelian randomization found a non-linear joint dose-response relationship between accelerometer-measured MVPA and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) with incident cardiovascular disease, showing greater benefits from combining both.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: More Than Just Arm Movement: Finger-Worn Accelerometers Provide a Valid and Sensitive Alternative to Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Measuring Real-World Upper-Limb Performance in Stroke Survivors
item.description: A cross-sectional observational study of 20 stroke survivors demonstrated that finger-worn accelerometers provide a valid and sensitive alternative to wrist-worn accelerometers for measuring real-world upper-limb motor performance, capturing more nuanced movements.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: A systematic review of early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers for post-stroke mobility prognostication.
item.description: This systematic review examined the prognostic capacity of early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers for mobility outcomes up to 24 months post-stroke, to help guide rehabilitation planning.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinically interpretable prediction models of stroke functional outcomes: A national cohort study of adults in inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the US.
item.description: A national retrospective cohort study (n=43,745) of US stroke patients in inpatient rehabilitation facilities developed clinically interpretable machine learning models to predict self-care and mobility function at discharge using IRF-PAI variables.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) demonstrated that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the dermal elastic coefficient and limb circumference in patients with severe hyper-dependency limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Incidence and risk factors for rotator cuff retear after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in middle-aged and older patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the incidence and risk factors for rotator cuff retear after arthroscopic repair in middle-aged and older patients.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Mental health in elite athletes: International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026)
item.description: The updated International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026) emphasizes that mental health symptoms and disorders are common in elite athletes, may be sport-related, and impact performance, recommending routine screening and monitoring.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Therapeutic Exercise Protocol During Hospitalization in Pediatric Oncohematological Patients: Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=30) found a therapeutic exercise program for hospitalized pediatric oncohematological patients improved quality of life, muscle strength, fatigue, and functional capacity compared to minimal active physiotherapy.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise prescription: Physiotherapy's most important and least standardized skill.
item.description: This commentary highlights that exercise prescription in musculoskeletal physiotherapy is a critical yet unstandardized skill, leading to inconsistencies in decision-making and communication, and calls for systematic approaches.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: When algorithms don't care: physiotherapy and the post-professional turn.
item.description: A perspective piece arguing that physiotherapy is entering a post-professional era due to late-stage capitalism, unbundling of professional claims, and digitally mediated technological disruption, which may marginalize practitioners in care delivery.
item.author: PubMed
